lead.headline: Trump says the India-US trade deal is 'pretty close' after Rubio and Jaishankar's talks in Mumbai, as Rubio urges India to buy more US energy and arms
lead.short: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that India and the United States are "pretty close" to a trade deal, and that it will be "a much different kind of deal". In Mumbai, Secretary of State Marco Rubio held talks with S. Jaishankar, and the foreign ministry said both sides welcomed progress on the Bilateral Trade Agreement.

why.text: A deal would settle the tariffs Indian exporters face in the US, and Rubio's requests point to larger Indian purchases of American oil, gas and defence equipment.

more: Rubio, on his second visit to India in under five months, told reporters before the meeting that "a small number of items are left to be wrapped up". He urged New Delhi to buy more American energy and defence equipment, called India a crude oil refining "superpower" and pressed for more Venezuelan crude to be processed in Indian refineries.

Jaishankar, after laying a wreath at the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, said India expects its partners to show "zero tolerance" towards terrorism. Rubio told The Indian Express that US ties with Pakistan or any other country "will never come at the expense" of the relationship with India.
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal met US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in Milwaukee and Washington earlier this month. Rubio visits Reliance's Jamnagar refinery on Wednesday.

update.new: The Mumbai talks took place; the MEA welcomed progress on the trade agreement and Trump said a deal was 'pretty close'.
update.front: A trade deal with the US is the biggest economic question in India this year, and both governments now say it is nearly done.

seconds.headline: Anthropic's draft IPO filing shows a net loss of more than $80bn in the first half of 2026, mostly accounting charges, the WSJ reports
seconds.short: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, recorded a net loss of more than $80bn in the first six months of 2026, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing a draft prospectus for its share sale. Most of it, $72bn, came from accounting charges on convertible notes and other instruments it issued to raise money.

why.text: Its share sale would be among the largest ever, and the disclosures are already lowering the valuation some investors discuss.

more: The loss compares with $13bn a year earlier. Revenue rose to $16.3bn in the six months to 30 June, from $1.1bn a year before, while spending on AI infrastructure nearly quadrupled to almost $9bn, the Journal said. Anthropic also indicated it could spend up to $750bn in the coming years on computing capacity, including deals under discussion.

Some investors at Anthropic's investor day in San Francisco last week discussed a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, Reuters reported, below the roughly $2 trillion previously expected for the November share sale. Reuters had reported in September that Anthropic lost $42bn in 2025.
The draft lists risks including how to stop its products causing harm through cyberattacks or blackmail by uncontrolled models. Anthropic did not comment.

update.new: First-half figures from the draft prospectus: a net loss of more than $80bn, mostly accounting charges.
update.front: The year's biggest AI listing now has its loss figure, and investors are already talking about a lower valuation.

seconds.headline: Musk says merging Tesla and SpaceX would be 'a good idea', and both companies have set up special committees to study it
seconds.short: Elon Musk said on Tuesday he is considering merging Tesla and SpaceX, his two biggest companies. Speaking on SpaceX's quarterly results call, he said special committees at both companies have been formed to examine a deal but have not agreed terms. Tesla is valued at about $1.5 trillion and SpaceX at $2 trillion.

why.text: A combination would be one of the largest mergers in history and would put Musk's rockets, satellites, AI and cars inside one listed company.

more: "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk told analysts, adding that a merger would need shareholder support and that there is "no guarantee" the committees will agree. "I do think there is a lot of merit to merging and a lot to be gained," he said.

SpaceX, which bought xAI and X before going public this year, now sells cloud computing capacity to companies including Anthropic and Google. That business brought in $7.5bn in the latest quarter and is its most profitable, while Starlink had revenue of $5.2bn. SpaceX as a whole has lost $1.1bn so far this year.
Tesla shares rose 2% after weeks of slight declines. Tesla reports its own quarterly results on Wednesday.

seconds.headline: Musk himself ordered the Starlink slowdown that grounded Ukraine's drones last week, the Wall Street Journal reports
seconds.short: Elon Musk ordered the slowdown of Starlink that hobbled Ukraine's army last week, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials. He capped the speeds at which Ukrainian terminals could stay connected, which made its attack and interceptor drones ineffective. Musk had earlier said such limits were decided by the US military and the president.

why.text: Ukraine's drone war against Russia runs on one company's satellites, and the report says the owner, not Washington, set the limits.

more: The Journal said Musk and Donald Trump discussed the decision in a phone call after the outage became public, and had discussed it before the restriction too. Both men have criticised Ukrainian attacks on Russian diesel refineries.

An adviser to Zelensky on military technology told The Guardian the limits led to several failed combat missions last week, and Zelensky said he felt betrayed and that "people would die". Last week Musk wrote on X that "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and POTUS"; Trump said he did not think either of them was responsible.
SpaceX says Starlink may be used only for civilian or defensive purposes. US envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in Russia to meet Vladimir Putin.

facts.source: Wall Street Journal, citing US officials

update.new: The WSJ reports Musk ordered the Starlink slowdown himself.
update.front: The report puts a private owner, not a government, behind a decision that changed the course of the war last week.

seconds.headline: France's parliament speaker proposes an inquiry into who organised Saturday's riots, as the prime minister blames far-left groups
seconds.short: Yaël Braun-Pivet, president of France's National Assembly, has proposed a parliamentary inquiry into the riots of 17 October and how they were organised. The prime minister has blamed far-left groups for planning some of the violence. A suspect has been arrested over the city hall fire, and the prime minister says curfews are working.

why.text: Ministers blame the far left and the far left denies it, and the argument now feeds campaigning for France's 2027 presidential election.

more: French intelligence told government circles this month that left-wing anarchist groups were involved in the student protests. A report dated 29 September and published by Le Figaro describes the "manipulation" of student demonstrations by unions and movements of the radical left, and suggests La France Insoumise was relying on violence as an electoral strategy before 2027. LFI denies this.

French television has repeatedly shown video from Saturday of young men in black, faces covered, attacking police vans with what look like hammers or machetes. Much of the looting appeared opportunistic while the violence looked planned, the BBC's Katya Adler reported from Paris, where shop windows are still smashed.

update.new: A parliamentary inquiry is proposed and a suspect is held over the city hall fire.
update.front: France's unrest has been Europe's biggest story for a week, and the question has turned to who planned it.

stories.headline: Pleas withdrawn: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka drop their Delhi High Court challenge after the judge questions it
stories.short: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka withdrew their Delhi High Court pleas against a magistrate's order extending their custody, after Justice Subramonium Prasad questioned why the court should hear them. He noted that their bond to keep the peace, given on 10 October, had allegedly been broken the very next day.

why.text: The case tests how far executive magistrates can keep protest leaders in custody, a power now under scrutiny.

more: The two had challenged a Special Executive Magistrate's 19 October order sending them to two more days in custody. Their counsel, Abhik Chimni, argued that the magistrate lacked jurisdiction. The judge said the High Court examines how a decision was made unless it is so perverse that it "shocks the conscience", and pointed them to an appeal against the order.

Told that Das and Ranka are 27 and 31, Justice Prasad asked, "So you're not Gen Z?" He said the protest had begun with students and young people but its cause appeared to be changing. "Suddenly they're talking about 'regime change', about 'ballot'," he said.
They are accused of breaching the bond a second time by trespassing at Jantar Mantar and waving a flag.

update.new: Das and Ranka withdrew their High Court pleas after the judge questioned them.

stories.headline: Both legs amputated: Australian MP Helen Haines is stable as the man accused of ramming her appears in court
stories.short: Doctors have amputated both legs of Helen Haines, the Australian independent MP hit repeatedly by a car outside her electorate office on Monday, her husband said. Brendan Nugent, 43, appeared in court in Wangaratta charged with intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving and causing harm to a federal official. He did not apply for bail.

why.text: The attack is described as an apparent act of political violence against a sitting federal MP.

more: Phil Haines said her left leg was amputated on Monday and her right on Wednesday, after doctors gave up hope of saving it. "The good news in all this is that Helen is alive and she's stable," he told reporters in Melbourne, adding that their 40th wedding anniversary is in November. The 65-year-old was flown to a Melbourne hospital by helicopter.

Nugent, from nearby Tarrawingee, entered no plea and will stay in custody until his next appearance in February. His lawyer, Chirag Patel, told the court his client may have mental health problems and a concussion, and has a rare spinal cord condition. Police have not given a motive.

update.new: Both legs have been amputated; the accused appeared in court.

Vinícius is banned for Sunday's Clásico at Camp Nou, and Mourinho may rotate some other starters to keep them fresh for that game.

why.text: Tonight's selection decides how fresh Madrid's best players are for Barcelona on Sunday.

more: Madrid's 24-man squad has Courtois, Lunin and Mestre in goal; Militão, Huijsen, Trent, Konaté, Cucurella, Carreras, Rüdiger and Dumfries in defence; Bellingham, Camavinga, Valverde, Tchouaméni, Arda Güler, Bernardo and Thiago in midfield; and Vinícius, Endrick, Mbappé, Espí, Brahim and Yan Diomande up front.

Real Madrid TV, the club's channel, has renewed its attack on Barcelona and the referees, saying Madrid will face "17 referees" at Camp Nou: the on-field officials, the fourth official, the VAR team and Barcelona's eleven players. It followed Ref Cam footage of Barcelona players asking for a VAR review of a Betis goal that was then ruled out.

stories.headline: India start a five-match T20I series in Christchurch on Thursday, with Bhuvneshwar Kumar back after nearly four years
stories.short: India play New Zealand in the first of five T20Is at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Thursday, starting at 12:30 IST, at the start of a long tour. Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 36, returns to India's T20I side after nearly four years away, and New Zealand's captain Mitchell Santner says the swing bowler will "love these conditions".

why.text: It starts a tour of five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests that runs to the end of November.

more: Santner named Bhuvneshwar as a threat because of how he moves the new ball in the air and off the pitch, and said it is "pretty challenging to be a bowler in India nowadays".

ESPNcricinfo says India arrive jet-lagged, with Shreyas Iyer's captaincy again in the spotlight, while New Zealand fans get a rare look at Finn Allen at home. The second match is also in Christchurch on Saturday, followed by Wellington on 27 October, Auckland on 30 October and Hamilton on 1 November.
The ODIs begin in Auckland on 4 November, and the first Test starts in Wellington on 19 November.
